nodes.name: Expressions and Statements
nodes.description: The distinction between expressions that evaluate to values and statements that perform actions, including assignment that binds names to values in a frame.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Expressions and Statements and Control Structures

nodes.name: Control Structures
nodes.description: Conditional statements and loops that direct which code executes and how often, controlling a program's flow based on boolean tests.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Expressions and Statements and Control Structures

nodes.name: Pure vs Non-Pure Functions
nodes.description: Pure functions that depend only on their arguments and return values without side effects, contrasted with non-pure functions that alter state or perform I/O.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Pure vs Non-Pure Functions and Environment Diagrams

nodes.name: Environment Diagrams
nodes.description: A model of execution tracking frames, bindings, and parent environments to explain how names resolve and how functions create local scopes.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram execution frames, variable bindings, and parent-environment links.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Pure vs Non-Pure Functions and Environment Diagrams

nodes.name: Functions as Arguments
nodes.description: Treating functions as first-class values by passing them as arguments, enabling higher-order functions that abstract over computational patterns.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Higher-Order Functions

nodes.name: Functions as Return Values
nodes.description: Returning functions from other functions, creating closures that capture enclosing variables to build configurable, stateful behaviour.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Higher-Order Functions

nodes.name: Lambda Expressions
nodes.description: Anonymous function expressions created with lambda, producing function values inline without binding them to a name.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Higher-Order Functions

nodes.name: Currying
nodes.description: Transforming a multi-argument function into a chain of single-argument functions, each returning another function until all arguments are supplied.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Currying and Decorators

nodes.name: Decorators
nodes.description: Higher-order functions applied with @ syntax that wrap another function to extend or modify its behaviour without changing its source.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Currying and Decorators

nodes.name: Sequences and Slicing
nodes.description: Ordered collections such as lists and strings supporting indexing and slicing to extract individual elements and subsequences by position.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Sequences and Slicing and List Comprehensions

nodes.name: List Comprehensions
nodes.description: A concise expression for constructing a list by transforming and optionally filtering elements drawn from an existing iterable.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Sequences and Slicing and List Comprehensions

nodes.name: Data Abstraction
nodes.description: Separating how data is used from how it is represented by defining constructors and selectors, isolating clients from representation changes.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Data Abstraction and Sequences

nodes.name: Dictionaries
nodes.description: A mutable mapping from unique keys to values supporting efficient lookup, insertion, and deletion by key rather than by position.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Data Abstraction and Sequences

nodes.name: Box-and-Pointer Diagrams
nodes.description: A diagram depicting lists and pairs as boxes containing pointers, visualising the structure, sharing, and mutation of compound data.
nodes.visual_hint: Box-and-pointer diagram of lists and pairs as boxes holding pointers.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Data Abstraction and Sequences

nodes.name: Recursion
nodes.description: A technique where a function calls itself on smaller subproblems, combining base cases and recursive cases so the computation terminates correctly.
nodes.visual_hint: Step through recursive calls accumulating and unwinding on the call stack.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Recursion and Tree Recursion

nodes.name: Tree Recursion
nodes.description: Recursion making multiple recursive calls per invocation, branching like a tree, as in computing Fibonacci numbers or counting partitions.
nodes.visual_hint: Draw the branching recursive calls as a recursion tree.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Recursion and Tree Recursion

nodes.name: Tree Data Abstraction
nodes.description: Representing tree structures using constructor and selector functions, hiding the underlying representation behind a data abstraction.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Tree Data Abstraction and Tree Traversal

nodes.name: Tree Traversal
nodes.description: Systematically visiting every node of a tree, typically via recursion, to process or aggregate the data the tree contains.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate visiting tree nodes in pre-order, in-order, and post-order.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Tree Data Abstraction and Tree Traversal

nodes.name: Mutability
nodes.description: The property of objects whose state can change after creation, introducing aliasing where multiple names refer to the same mutable object.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Mutability and Object-Oriented Programming

nodes.name: Object-Oriented Programming
nodes.description: A paradigm organising programs around objects that bundle state and behaviour, defined by classes with attributes and methods.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Mutability and Object-Oriented Programming

nodes.name: Inheritance and Composition
nodes.description: Two reuse mechanisms: inheritance deriving subclasses that specialise a base class, and composition assembling objects from other objects.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Inheritance and Composition, Class and Instance Attributes, and String Representation

nodes.name: Class and Instance Attributes
nodes.description: The difference between class attributes shared by all instances of a class and instance attributes stored separately on each object.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Inheritance and Composition, Class and Instance Attributes, and String Representation

nodes.name: String Representation
nodes.description: Defining how objects display through __str__ for readable output and __repr__ for unambiguous, often reconstructable representations.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Inheritance and Composition, Class and Instance Attributes, and String Representation

nodes.name: Linked Lists
nodes.description: A recursive structure of nodes each holding a value and a reference to the next, supporting sequential access and structural sharing.
nodes.visual_hint: Box-and-pointer chain of nodes linked by next references.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Linked Lists and Mutable Trees

nodes.name: Mutable Trees
nodes.description: Tree structures whose nodes can be modified in place, allowing branches and values to change after the tree is constructed.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Linked Lists and Mutable Trees

nodes.name: Iterators
nodes.description: Objects implementing the iterator protocol with __iter__ and __next__, producing elements one at a time and raising StopIteration when exhausted.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Iterators and Generators

nodes.name: Generators
nodes.description: Functions using yield to lazily produce a sequence of values on demand, suspending and resuming their state between successive calls.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Iterators and Generators

nodes.name: Scheme Syntax
nodes.description: Scheme's parenthesised prefix notation, where every expression is an atom or a list whose first element names the operator or special form.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Scheme Syntax and Scheme Lists and Pairs

nodes.name: Scheme Lists and Pairs
nodes.description: Scheme's fundamental pairs built with cons and accessed by car and cdr, composed to form lists and other recursive structures.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Scheme Syntax and Scheme Lists and Pairs

nodes.name: Tail Calls and Optimization
nodes.description: Calls in tail position whose results are returned directly, letting interpreters reuse stack frames so recursion runs in constant space.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Tail Calls and Optimization and Macros

nodes.name: Macros
nodes.description: Scheme macros that transform unevaluated source expressions into new code before evaluation, extending the language with new syntactic forms.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Tail Calls and Optimization and Macros

nodes.name: Lexical Analysis and Parsing
nodes.description: Converting program text into structured form by lexical analysis into tokens followed by parsing into an abstract syntax tree.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Lexical Analysis and Parsing and Evaluation Process

nodes.name: Evaluation Process
nodes.description: The interpreter step that evaluates an expression in an environment, recursively reducing it to a value according to evaluation rules.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Lexical Analysis and Parsing and Evaluation Process

nodes.name: Application Process
nodes.description: The interpreter step that applies a procedure to evaluated arguments by binding parameters in a new frame and evaluating the body.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Application Process and Exceptions

nodes.name: Exceptions
nodes.description: A control-flow mechanism for signalling and handling errors by raising exceptions that propagate up the call stack until caught by a handler.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Application Process and Exceptions

nodes.name: Regular Expressions
nodes.description: A notation describing text patterns used to search, match, and extract substrings using character classes, quantifiers, and grouping.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Regular Expressions and BNF Context-Free Grammars

nodes.name: BNF Context-Free Grammars
nodes.description: Backus-Naur Form, a notation for context-free grammars that specifies a language's syntax through production rules over terminals and non-terminals.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: Regular Expressions and BNF Context-Free Grammars

nodes.name: SQL Tables and Queries
nodes.description: Declarative SQL queries that select, filter, and order rows from tables to retrieve data without specifying procedural steps.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: SQL Tables and Queries and SQL Joins and Aggregation

nodes.name: SQL Joins and Aggregation
nodes.description: Combining rows from multiple tables on related columns and summarising groups with aggregate functions such as count, sum, and average.

evidence_refs.locator: Summer 2026 course schedule/textbook unit: SQL Tables and Queries and SQL Joins and Aggregation
